Collection Guidelines

  1. Run AR Aging Reports regularly.
  2. Follow up with phone calls, text and email.
  3. Focus on 1–30 days past due — you have the highest chance of collection here.
  4. Make an Alternative Arrangement (AA) as soon as trouble is sensed.
  5. Come up with a realistic plan for the RP.
  6. If AA is broken, change appointment to Deb/Finish and send certified and regular postal letters.
  7. If a situation, such as job loss, has caused financial difficulties that make it challenging to continue orthodontic treatment, it may be appropriate to discuss the possibility of discontinuing (D/C) treatment with Dr. Akhavan.
Treatment does not progress on patients with a past due balance that does not have a plan for resolution. One appointment will be made for Re-tie/Hygiene check. If an AA is not made at or by that appointment, the next visit may be DEB.

Policy Rules

  1. Must be employed at the referring practice for a minimum of 6 months before courtesies become active.
  2. Only two staff members per office can be in treatment at the same time.
  3. If employment ends, monthly rate reverts to the standard (non-discounted) rate retroactive to last date of employment.
  4. Not transferable — the discount is tied exclusively to the specific referring office listed on the agreement.
  5. Referral status is based on referrals from the previous 12 months.
  6. When multiple discounts apply (e.g., sibling), only the larger discount applies.
  7. Discounts apply to non-surgical orthodontic treatment except Invisalign & Next Level Aligners (separate discounted fee).
  8. Verify employment status with the referring office before completing this form.
  9. Keep a signed copy in the patient's financial file.

Orthodontic Status Letter — Military Service
For patients enlisting or commissioning in any branch — Air Force, Space Force, Army, Navy, Marines, Coast Guard, Guard or Reserve. Prints a letter on letterhead for Dr. Akhavan to sign stating that treatment is complete, that it ended early so the patient can enlist, or that the patient is still in treatment with a firm date the appliances will be off. Worded to the military’s medical entry standard for braces and aligners.

Patient

Treatment

Branch & Recipient

Fills in from the entry path. Clear it to open the letter with “To Whom It May Concern” only.

Retainers

Doctor & Statement

Office contact info (address, phone, website) prints under the signature.

Military Letter Guidelines

  1. Dr. Akhavan signs every copy. It is a clinical certification — staff prepare it, the doctor reviews and signs.
  2. Pick the status that is true today. Braces or clear aligners in active use disqualify an applicant. Retainers — bonded or removable — do not.
  3. Still in treatment: the military accepts our written commitment that active treatment ends before the patient is sworn in. Get the ship / report date from the patient or recruiter, set the projected end date before it, and book the debond now.
  4. Ended early: before the debond, have the patient — or a parent if under 18 — sign the Removal Waiver (Discontinuation folder).
  5. Two copies print. The Next Level Copy is scanned to the chart; the unlabeled copy is the patient’s original for the recruiter or MEPS.
  6. The letter carries the patient’s SSN. Hand it to the patient — don’t fax or email it to a recruiter unless the patient (a parent, if a minor) has authorized that in writing.
The wording follows DoD Instruction 6130.03, Vol. 1 — the medical standard for entering the military. Active orthodontic appliances, fixed or removable (including clear aligners), are disqualifying unless the appliance is a retainer, or an orthodontist documents that active treatment will be finished before the applicant is sworn in to active duty. Service academy applicants may have an earlier DoDMERB deadline (often June 1) — confirm it before promising a date.

Privacy Practices & Photo/Records Release
Combined HIPAA-compliant form: (1) Authorization to release patient photos and records, and (2) Acknowledgement of receipt of Notice of Privacy Practices. Print for signature at intake or when consent is needed.

Patient Info

Photo & Records Authorization

Patient/RP will select Yes or No for each on the printed form.

  1. Display photos within the office to show positive outcomes
  2. Display photos on the office website and social media (e.g., before/after, contest winners)
  3. Use records/photos for professional consultations, research, education, or publication

Authorized Individuals for Record Disclosure

Names of individuals the patient authorizes NLO to share medical record info, appointment details, and financial information with (written on printed form).

FC Reminders

  1. Give patient/RP a copy of the current Notice of Privacy Practices.
  2. Explain each photo consent option — patient can say Yes or No to each independently.
  3. Signing is voluntary — refusal does not affect treatment.
  4. Patient may revoke authorization at any time in writing.
  5. Authorization expires when the patient is no longer a patient of NLO, unless revoked sooner.
  6. If patient refuses to sign NPP acknowledgement, document the reason in the Office Use section.

HIPAA Compliance Notes

  1. 45 CFR 164.508 — Authorization must include: description of info, who discloses, who receives, purpose, expiration, signature/date, right to revoke, treatment not conditioned on signing, and redisclosure warning.
  2. Fla. Stat. 456.057 — Florida requires written authorization for any disclosure. Third parties cannot re-disclose without patient’s express written consent.
  3. 2026 NPP Update — As of Feb 16, 2026, NPP must address substance use disorder (SUD) record protections per 42 CFR Part 2 alignment.
  4. Photos are PHI even outside the medical record if they can identify a patient.
  5. Maintain a log of all disclosures per Florida law.

Delivery Record (office use)

Before You Send This

  1. Dr. Akhavan approves every one of these. Ending care is his call, not a front-desk decision.
  2. Confirm the AA is truly broken — check the ledger for a payment that posted late or a draft that was retried before assuming default.
  3. Try one documented live conversation first. A letter that follows a real phone call holds up far better than one that follows silence.
  4. Mail it both ways: certified with return receipt and regular first-class. Certified alone fails when they simply refuse the envelope; the first-class copy is what proves it was reasonably delivered.
  5. Record the certified tracking number above and file the signed green card with the chart when it comes back.
  6. Keep seeing them for true emergencies only during the window — loose bracket, poking wire, pain. No adjustments, no progression. Log every emergency visit.
  7. Push hard to get the debond scheduled inside the window. Appliances left on unsupervised are the real liability, not the unpaid balance.
  8. Do not withhold records over money. Florida law (Fla. Stat. §456.057) requires copies be furnished on written request; a reasonable copying charge is allowed. Withholding records because of a balance is where offices get in trouble.
Have the practice’s attorney read this letter once before its first use, and re-check it if the office ever changes its fee proration method or collection vendor. It is written to be protective, but it is a template — not legal advice.
Sequence reminder: Altered Arrangement → broken → appointment changed to Deb/Finish → this letter. If the hardship is genuine (job loss, illness), talk to Dr. Akhavan about a D/C instead — that path keeps the relationship intact.

UF Referral Steps

  1. Add the patient, the reason and the surgeon (or First Available). Our office details are already on it.
  2. Extractions: tap every tooth on the chart. UF asks for each tooth — never “All.”
  3. Print or Download PDF, then fax it to UF Oral Surgery at 352-294-8089, or mail it to P.O. Box 100416, Gainesville, FL 32610-0416.
  4. Send the patient’s chart notes and diagnostic reports with it — UF asks for them with every referral.
  5. Radiographs: email the pan / CBCT to Xraysoralsurgery@dental.ufl.edu by secure (encrypted) email, or have the patient bring them.
  6. Questions: UF clinic 352-273-6731 or 352-273-6733 · Finance & Insurance 352-273-6725.

Insurance policies are a contract between you and your insurance company. We will file claims on your behalf as a courtesy. We accept assignment on primary insurance claims and allow the insurance company to make payment installments throughout orthodontic treatment. You are not expected to pay the expected primary insurance unless the claim is denied or altered due to a cancellation or change of the policy. You will be responsible for any expected insurance portion that is not paid by the primary insurance company.

Secondary insurance will be filed and any payments will be credited towards your balance in our office. Any secondary insurance payments that are in excess of the total treatment fee will be refunded to you upon completion of treatment.

Secondary insurance usually pays 50% of your expected out of pocket after the primary insurance has paid. You will have out of pocket expense even with secondary insurance. Monthly payments will continue as stated on your financial agreement until your balance is paid in full.

If you have any questions, please call.

Please note you must carry an active policy for the duration of orthodontic treatment to utilize your total lifetime benefits.

Notice of Termination of Care

Sent via Certified Mail, Return Receipt Requested and by First-Class U.S. Mail

RE: — Termination of Care and Final Notice of Account Default

Because that arrangement has not been maintained, Dr. Akhavan is withdrawing from the further care of , and the doctor–patient relationship with Next Level Orthodontics will end on .

Emergency Care Only for the Next Days

Through , this office will remain available to for emergency care only. Emergency care means relief of pain or discomfort caused by the orthodontic appliances — a loose or broken bracket or band, a poking or displaced wire, or a similar problem requiring urgent attention. Routine adjustments, wire changes, progress visits, and any further advancement of orthodontic treatment will not be provided. To be seen for an emergency during this period, call the office at (352) 332-7466 during business hours.

Appliance Removal (Debond) Must Be Completed Within This Period

You must schedule and complete an appliance removal appointment on or before . There is no charge for the removal appointment itself. After that date, Next Level Orthodontics will not see for any purpose, including appliance removal.

Orthodontic appliances left in place without professional supervision can cause serious harm, including decalcification and permanent white-spot lesions, tooth decay, inflammation and disease of the gums and supporting bone, shortening of the tooth roots (root resorption), and movement of the teeth into unintended and unwanted positions. If the appliances are not removed by this office within the period above, you must promptly arrange for their removal by another licensed dentist or orthodontist at your own expense, and you accept responsibility for any consequences of leaving them in place.

Retainers Are Not Included

No retainers or other retention appliances will be fabricated, delivered, or monitored by this office, and no retention phase will be provided. Because treatment is ending before it is complete, the position of the teeth is not final or stable and should be expected to change. The result achieved to date is not a completed orthodontic result and this office makes no representation that it will be maintained.

Account Summary

Total Contract Fee
Fee Earned for Treatment Rendered to Date
Total Paid to Date
Balance Now Due

The amount shown as earned reflects the orthodontic services actually provided through the date of this letter, not the full remaining contract balance. Credit has been given for all payments received.

Payment of the balance shown above is due in full on or before .

If the balance is not paid in full by that date, the account will be turned over to our attorney or to a collection agency for collection, consistent with the Financial Responsibility Agreement signed at the start of treatment. You may also be responsible for the costs of collection, including reasonable attorney’s fees and court costs, to the extent permitted by law, and the delinquency may be reported to a consumer reporting agency.

Our records show payments received exceed the fee earned for treatment rendered. No payment is being demanded by this letter. Please contact the office regarding the credit balance shown above.

Future Treatment at This Office

Please also understand that neither nor any other patient for whom you are the responsible party will be accepted for treatment at Next Level Orthodontics in the future. This applies to new treatment, re-treatment, retention, and any resumption of the treatment ended by this letter, and it applies whether or not the balance described above is later paid.

Continuing Care Elsewhere

We strongly encourage you to place under the care of another orthodontist without delay so that treatment can be properly completed or properly discontinued. You may obtain the names of other orthodontists in this area from your general dentist, from your dental insurance carrier, or from the American Association of Orthodontists at aaoinfo.org.

Upon your signed written request, a copy of ’s orthodontic records, including radiographs, will be furnished to you or forwarded to the treating provider of your choice in accordance with Florida law. A reasonable charge for copying may apply. Records will not be withheld because of any balance owed.

This letter is the office’s final notice regarding this account. If you believe the amounts shown above are incorrect, notify the office in writing within ten (10) days of the date of this letter so the account can be reviewed. Nothing in this letter waives any right of Next Level Orthodontics, all of which are expressly reserved.

Sincerely,
